sources.title: Regression Discontinuity Designs
sources.version: Annual Review of Economics 14 (2022), 821–851; author-hosted published version
verified_scope: Sharp treatment rule and local continuity identification; absence of common support at an exact score.
Local-randomization window requires its own assignment and outcome exclusion restrictions.
Fuzzy treatment versus assignment effects; different complier conventions require explicit continuity/exclusion/monotonicity conditions.
cautions: Do not equate continuity with a randomized finite window or use observed balance/density tests as proof of unobserved continuity.
Use an explicitly specified constant-near-cutoff compliance-type sufficient model; the review surveys several distinct fuzzy definitions.
The chapter must define its own probability law rather than import the review’s differing uses of Fisher/Neyman terminology.
sources.not_adopted: General fuzzy inference, extrapolation, multidimensional/discrete-score extensions, software behavior and later uninspected sections.
sources.chapter_use: Sharp continuity targets and the separate local-randomization framework; fuzzy assignment, receipt, exclusion and monotonicity under the chapter's explicit common cutoff-type population. Original sorting and observational-equivalence examples prove their own claims.
sources.verification: Exact scoped primary inspection reused from root preparation; author read the complete preparation record and independently derived the original chapter cases. No new full-document or uninspected-appendix reading claimed.

sources.title: A Practical Introduction to Regression Discontinuity Designs: Foundations
sources.version: arXiv:1911.09511v1, 21 November 2019; manuscript title dated 22 November 2019; the subsequent 2020 book is not substituted for this inspected body
verified_scope: Separate side-local polynomial weighted regressions, raw observations, cutoff intercept difference, kernel/order/bandwidth roles.
Smoothing bias and estimation/inference bandwidth distinction; bias correction must account for randomness and covariance of the estimated correction.
Density diagnostics and the separately assumed exact binomial experiment.
cautions: A fixed fractional reduction of an MSE-optimal bandwidth does not by itself make standardized leading bias vanish. The original fixed-grid proof will show that undersmoothing requires a rate condition, not merely a smaller number.
Do not infer universal finite-sample variance ordering, superiority, coverage or software guarantees from the monograph’s asymptotic discussion. Prove only explicit known-Gaussian local calculations.

Continuity of density does not establish potential-outcome continuity; absence of rejection is not no-manipulation identification. Exact finite-window binomial validity requires its declared probability law.
Empirical examples and commands are contextual source text, not reproduced or independently validated.
sources.not_adopted: No general robust-bias-correction theorem, automatic bandwidth implementation, cluster/nonparametric coverage refinement or empirical application audit.
sources.chapter_use: Separate-side local-polynomial weights, smoothing bias, estimated-correction uncertainty and the limitations of density diagnostics. The original fixed-score known-Gaussian proof establishes only its own finite coverage and rate calculations.
sources.verification: Exact scoped primary inspection reused from root preparation; author read the complete preparation record and independently derived the original chapter cases. No new full-document or uninspected-appendix reading claimed.

sources.author: Alberto Abadie
sources.title: Using Synthetic Controls: Feasibility, Data Requirements, and Methodological Aspects
sources.version: Journal of Economic Literature 59(2), June 2021, 391–425; MIT author-hosted final published body
verified_scope: Treatment/counterfactual definition, nonnegative simplex weights and preperiod-only predictor criterion.
Linear common-factor logic and limits of good prefit, too many donors, long preperiods and interpolation.
Refitted in-space placebo gaps, post/preRMSPE, inclusive treated-unit rank and actual versus benchmark assignment law.
Donor spillovers, convex-hull support, preperiod holdout/backdating and leave-one-donor diagnostics.
cautions: Page6 occasionally calls weights positive; feasible simplex includes zero weights, as preceding definition/formula state.
The general stochastic bias theorem and original2010appendix are not proved/read here; use an original finite noiseless factor/rank proof and explicit counterexamples.
Perfect prefit alone does not imply future-factor support; nonunique weights can produce different forecasts.
A zero preRMSPE needs explicit handling; do not divide by zero. Uniform placebo ranks have design validity only for the stipulated assignment law, otherwise are a benchmark comparison.
Excluding possible spillover donors addresses a stated threat and may worsen support; it does not prove absence of all interference.
sources.not_adopted: No German reunification or other empirical effect validation, general stochastic bias bound, automatic sparse/unique optimizer, observational randomization guarantee, conformal or later extension theorem.
sources.chapter_use: Preperiod simplex fitting, convex support, factor logic, donor contamination, holdouts and fully refitted placebo comparisons. Original finite noiseless rank proofs and actual-law inclusive-rank calculations replace any unproved general theorem.
sources.verification: Exact scoped primary inspection reused from root preparation; author read the complete preparation record and independently derived the original chapter cases. No new full-document or uninspected-appendix reading claimed.

cautions_applied: A continuous version plus positive two-sided support defines the cutoff target; P(R=0)=0 does not assign an arbitrary conditional value a causal interpretation.
Density continuity and nonrejection do not establish potential-outcome continuity or a finite-window random assignment law. The sorting counterexample proves this directly.

Estimated correction variance and covariance are both computed. The covariance is exactly zero only in the stated three-distance equal-weight design; the correction still increases variance from 14σ²/3 to 38σ².

The fixed-grid sequence has n observations available per side. A fixed fraction of the MSE-optimal width leaves nonzero standardized bias; proper undersmoothing requires a rate condition and sufficient local observations.

Finite normal coverage uses fixed scores, predetermined widths, independent Gaussian noise and known variance. Curvature-bound intervals require the stated deterministic derivative bounds; no general robust-bias-correction result is imported.
Fuzzy RD uses a fully specified constant-near-cutoff type population with continuous type-conditional means. Direct assignment effects and defiers break exclusion and monotonicity respectively.

Synthetic-control weights are nonnegative, including zero. A unique fitted predictor need not give unique weights or a unique causal counterfactual; a prespecified tie rule resolves an algorithmic ambiguity only.

Factor proofs use noiseless untreated training outcomes and unaffected donors. Full pre-factor rank or an explicitly derived future-row-space restriction is substantive. A post-only factor invalidates an extrapolation claim despite perfect prefit.
The interval from all optimal weights is a sharp identified interval only with a maintained fixed donor-mixture restriction; otherwise it is an algorithmic forecast range.

All candidate placebo labels are refitted. Known actual assignment probabilities and the sharp null justify inclusive rank validity, including ties and declared zero-RMSPE handling. Uniform observational comparisons do not automatically inherit exact calibration.
not_inspected_or_adopted: General RBC, unknown-variance bandwidth-selection coverage, clustering refinements or current software behavior.
